title: Kingdom of Iraq
capsule: The Hashemite Kingdom of Iraq attained full independence on 3 October 1932 as the first Arab state to join the League of Nations, though Faisal I's British-assisted accession in 1921 marks its actual founding. Faisal I navigated between tribal, Sunni, Shia, Kurdish, and Assyrian constituencies until his death in 1933; his son Ghazi I promoted pan-Arab nationalism until a suspicious car accident ended his life in 1939. The young Faisal II ruled under his uncle Abd al-Ilah as regent until 1953, during which the kingdom joined the Baghdad Pact in 1955. On 14 July 1958, General Abd al-Karim Qasim led a coup that killed both Faisal II and Abd al-Ilah, abolished the monarchy, and proclaimed the Republic of Iraq.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Kingdom of Iraq's boundaries and political history are well-documented through British mandate records, League of Nations materials, and Iraqi government archives; the northern Kurdish frontier and Mosul's incorporation after the 1926 League ruling are clear.
